parallel.requirements: Recognized that the prompt required a from-scratch behavioral reimplementation of the Melody CLI by running the provided executable and reading bundled docs only.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Created exploratory tasks plus an implementation task, then launched one workflow with many probe agents and later critics before parent implementation work.
parallel.implementation: Performed many local probes and eventually wrote Cargo.toml and compile.sh, but did not create src/main.rs or a working reimplementation before timeout.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Submitted an artifact containing scaffold files, corpus data, notes, original assets, and the original executable, but no source implementation tree.
parallel.verification: The available verification was exploratory probing; official evaluation completed with compile_failed and 1438 tests not run.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with the workflow killed and only build scaffolding present, leaving the executable behavior unreimplemented.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same reverse-engineering prompt and probed behavior directly from README, assets, CLI flags, grammar, literals, colors, and REPL cases.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in the single parent trajectory with no workflow calls, no task outputs, and no child logs.
serial.implementation: Collected extensive behavioral observations but did not write source files, compile script, or replacement executable before timeout.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Submitted only the original skeleton materials and assets; artifact validation was not ok and no reimplementation files were packaged.
serial.verification: Ran many direct local probes of the executable but no integrated tests of a new implementation because none was produced.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out during further CLI/REPL probing and official evaluation also compile_failed with 1438 tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received and initially followed the prompt requiring original source based on observed executable behavior only.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the identical prompt and likewise probed the provided executable and documentation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition difference is evidenced; both failed despite recognizing the same core task obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created separate tasks for grammar, CLI, corpus, and Rust implementation, then launched a broad workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation or subagents and kept exploration in one parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split the work into a large concurrent probe plan; serial remained single-threaded and avoided child ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts asked for report files and probe findings rather than interoperating code interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child handoffs or interface contracts because all observations stayed in the parent context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is not a missing interface contract; parallel context transfer happened as report-oriented fan-out, while serial avoided handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel began implementation only at the end by writing Cargo.toml and compile.sh for a Rust binary path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing CLI and REPL behavior until timeout and never wrote a source or build scaffold.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced minimal build scaffolding but no actual implementation source; serial produced no implementation files at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflow ended killed and aborted, so its broad probe/critic lifecycle never returned as a completed basis for implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it ended while a local probe command was killed by timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unfinished child-workflow lifecycle; serial had only unfinished local command activity and no join boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel artifact included notes, corpus, Cargo.toml, compile.sh, assets, and original executable, but no implementation source tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact contained only original repository files, assets, and original executable and artifact validation was not ok.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither integrated a usable final implementation; parallel added scaffold and generated notes/corpus while serial delivered only the original skeleton.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had exploratory probe evidence but no successful build or integrated acceptance before official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had many direct executable probes but no new implementation to verify, and official evaluation also compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked end-to-end verification of a submitted reimplementation; the official result was the same compile failure in both modes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after 513 tool calls, one workflow, 20 child logs, and 964900 workflow child tokens.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with no workflow tasks and no workflow child tokens.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed a large share of budget through concurrent child workflow breadth, while serial consumed the budget in direct local probing.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed evaluation is not discordant: both modes failed with compile_failed and 0/1438 tests run. The process difference is that parallel exhausted substantial budget in a broad child workflow before reaching implementation scaffold, whereas serial spent the entire window on local probing and never wrote implementation files.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out and child-token consumption displaced implementation time before any src/main.rs was written.
serial_contributors: Serial local probing also failed to transition into implementation before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel submitted minimal Rust build scaffold without source; serial submitted no build scaffold or source.
evaluator_effects: Both current official evaluations completed and report compile_failed with all 1438 tests not run.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported adverse parallel process contrast only

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly created Task #4 for a dependency-free Rust reimplementation, so implementation ownership existed even though it did not complete.
No multiple completed component implementations existed that needed an unowned reconciliation step.
The late problem was not an unowned final placement of complete components; there was no complete source tree to assemble.
The workflow and parent retained end-to-end responsibility; the failure was budget exhaustion before implementation, not an absent pipeline owner.
There was no single mandatory serial preflight gate; the delay came from a broad parallel probe workflow and critics.
The investigation was parallel fan-out, not investigators completed as one serial first phase before implementation.
Although implementation started too late, the more specific observed allocation boundary is collective fan-out and workflow budget exhaustion.

The parallel parent launched a broad workflow that ran 13 agents and then consumed the remaining budget in an aborted/killed state. The parent only reached scaffold files near timeout, so the required implementation path was displaced before closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: The indispensable implementation window was consumed by workflow fan-out, leaving only Cargo.toml and compile.sh scaffolding and no buildable src/main.rs before official compile evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing takeover was downstream of the same aborted broad workflow and does not provide a different corrective boundary or consequence from reducing and bounding the fan-out.

candidates.reason: No single child assignment is shown to dominate the failure; the adverse episode is aggregate breadth across many children and critics.
The child prompts included the benchmark constraints and requested precise reports; no known requirement omitted from an initial child brief is tied to unusable work.
The delegated work produced reports, not separately owned interoperating code components with conflicting contracts.
No specific known finding is proven to disappear between actors and cause repeated or wrong work.
Large reports and many notes were possible, but the run ended before a parent decision point that visibly failed because present information was too bulky to reduce.
No receiver acted on a superseded requirement, workspace state, or stale handoff.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts are shown reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; the run timed out with an incomplete scaffold and failed evaluation.
The workflow had stalled or retried children, but there is no concrete replacement that repeated prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints.

No delegated implementation was completed or retrievable for the parent to adopt; children were probe/report workers.

The children wrote notes/reports and corpus outputs; no concrete unstable final implementation provenance problem arose from shared implementation writes.
